The United States, after listening to the citizens of it's territories, has decided that alongside Hong Kong in 2035, Puerto Rico will have the ability to vote for it's own Statehood. The requests for a Statehood vote have not fallen on deaf ears, however we need to take care of some things in Puerto Rico before it reaches statehood.

Congress will vote on whether or not to allow Puerto Rico to file Super Chapter 9 bankruptcy to help clear Puerto Rico of it's $72 billion debt crisis. As of right now, Chapter 9 bankruptcy is only available to cities and public organizations - neither of which Puerto Rico would qualify for. This vote would allow Puerto Rico to declare bankruptcy as a territory and the United States would help fund a plan to help pay off it's debts and stabilize it's local government. From there, in 2035, the citizens would be able to vote for their right to become the 52nd state in the Union.

Both issues were discussed at a hearing on Puerto Rico's $72 billion debt crisis, held on Thursday by the U.S. Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. However, the vote on whether or not to allow the territory to file for bankruptcy will be held later this month.
